open_issues: OWNER DECISION — A02 «تذكر هذا الجهاز ٨ ساعات»: still not built, and I recommend it stays unbuilt. Remembering the session means wrapping the admin.db key to the machine (DPAPI), so whoever carries the computer away opens the organisation's signing keys without the password. Either the design drops the tick box or the owner accepts that trade.

OWNER DECISION — A01 recovery sheet: the design draws twelve 8-character one-time codes; the B1 specification and Wakeel.Crypto's RecoveryCode both define a single 20-character code, and the build follows the specification (one code plus its QR). The image needs re-cutting or the specification needs changing.

OWNER DECISION — A02 lock-out wording: the design's standing note says «يُقفل الدخول ١٥ دقيقة بعد ٥ محاولات خاطئة»; the build follows the specification's «٣٠ ثانية تتضاعف». Specification currently wins, but the image and the product disagree.

Audit detail names: the guard now decides by whole name segments, which cannot separate «officeKey» (key material) from «office_code» (a label) on the reviewer's suggested rule alone — the reviewer's own two acceptance cases contradict each other, since «key_version» begins with the segment «key». I resolved it with a documented domain rule (a trailing «key» segment is material unless followed by a metadata word; «code» is a label unless it stands alone) and made every match redact rather than throw. admin-2 and admin-3 should read AdminAuditService.LooksLikeSecret before choosing detail names.
notes:
Every finding is fixed, and each fix is covered by a test or verified in the running host.

MEDIUM 1 — AdminAccountService.Create() storage gap. The catch filter now also takes Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException (matching SignIn and Recover), and a new SetAsideOrphanedDatabase() runs immediately before _db.Open: when admin.db exists with no key file beside it, nothing in it can ever be opened again, so it is renamed to admin.db.orphaned-<timestamp> (deleted only if the rename fails) and the retry the screen offers can actually succeed. Two tests: Create_SucceedsWhenAnInterruptedRunLeftADatabaseWithNoKeyFileBesideIt (writes 4 KB of random bytes to admin.db, asserts creation works and the stray file was set aside) and Create_RefusesInWordsRatherThanThrowingWhenTheFolderCannotBeWrittenTo (a directory where the database file belongs — exactly the case that used to throw SqliteException out of the render; it now returns StorageFailed).

MEDIUM 2 — A03 alerts sub-line. The panel no longer prints AlertOfficeNoSetup unconditionally. It counts the alerts by kind and renders AdminAr.Dashboard.AlertsSummary(offices, changes, revoked) inside <Bdi>, naming only the kinds that are present («مكتبان بانتظار ملف الإعداد · تغيير بانتظار التوزيع · جهاز مُلغى», built from the existing Counting helpers plus a new Counting.Changes). Two tests: a text test over the four combinations, and a bUnit test that seeds an office whose only alert is a revoked device and asserts the panel head says «جهاز مُلغى» and does NOT contain «ملف الإعداد».

MEDIUM 3 — audit detail keys. SerializeDetails no longer substring-matches and no longer throws. AdminAuditService.LooksLikeSecret splits the key into segments (at _ - . space and camel-case boundaries) and matches whole segments; anything it flags has its VALUE replaced by «—» while the row is still written, because a log line must never kill a screen action. office_code and key_version keep their values; password, newPassword, recoveryCode, officeKey, private_key, seed, token, wrap, passphrase and a bare «code» are redacted. Two tests replace the old throw test, including the reviewer's two acceptance cases asserted exactly.

LOW 4 — A02 oversize image now shows the new AdminAr.Account.Recovery.ImageTooLarge instead of ImageNoCode.
LOW 5 — A01 dead ternary removed; step one shows a new Create.CreateHint («أكمل الحقول ثم أنشئ الحساب.») and StartHint is left to the sheet. Confirmed live: the footer read the new hint before creation and switched to StartHint after.
LOW 6 — AlertsAll is now rendered as a text button in the alerts panel head (with tooltip), navigating through AdminRoutes.ForTab(AdminAr.Tabs.AuditLog), inert until admin-3 adds A11 — the same pattern the export button already uses. Asserted in the bUnit test.
LOW 7 — new AdminDashboardService.ReadOrgLine() returns AdminOrgLine (org name + the three figures) in one grouped query; AdminLayout.OnParametersSet calls it instead of Read(). A test asserts the narrow query and the full board never drift apart, and that a locked tool returns AdminOrgLine.Empty.
LOW 8 — AdminHostPaths no longer grants BUILTIN\Users Modify over the whole tool root. The grant now applies only to exports\, staging\ and logs\; keys\ and admin.db keep the access list they inherit. Verified on disk after the live run: exports\ carries an explicit non-inherited BUILTIN\Users Modify entry, keys\ carries none.
LOW 9 — the stray duplicate <summary> block is gone; the doc now sits on the field it describes and the class remarks say redact rather than refuse.
LOW 10 — recoveryCode.KeyMaterial is wiped in the same finally as the database key, after the QR and the grouped display have been built.

TWO DESIGN ITEMS ALSO BUILT: the sheet now carries «رقم الورقة» (of the form 20260916/10540 — the issue day plus a cryptographically random five-digit serial, unrelated to the code, tested for shape and for not containing the code) and a «طُبعت dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm» chip that appears once the sheet has gone to the printer. The sheet number is also written to the «admin.recovery.issued» audit row under the detail name sheet_number, which incidentally exercises the new guard.
